subject: Biochemistry
vignette: A 34-year-old woman is evaluated after a routine screening shows an HDL cholesterol level of 18 mg/dL. She has no symptoms, and her fasting LDL cholesterol and triglycerides are normal. Plasma studies show markedly reduced cholesteryl ester formation and low lecithin-cholesterol acyltransferase (LCAT) activity. Her brother has a similar lipid profile.
question: Deficiency of which of the following apolipoproteins most directly explains the reduced LCAT activity in this patient?
explanation_correct: Apolipoprotein A-I is found only on alpha-lipoproteins (HDL) and is the physiologic activator of LCAT, the enzyme that esterifies most of the cholesterol in plasma and is required for HDL maturation. Loss of apo A-I function therefore lowers cholesteryl ester formation and HDL cholesterol. No other major apolipoprotein activates LCAT.

explanation_incorrect.A: Apo B-100 is the ligand for the LDL receptor on liver-derived particles and does not activate LCAT.
explanation_incorrect.B: Apo C-II is a cofactor for lipoprotein lipase, which hydrolyzes triglycerides in circulating chylomicrons and VLDL.
explanation_incorrect.D: Apo E mediates hepatic uptake of chylomicron remnants, VLDL, IDL, and HDL; it is not an LCAT activator.
explanation_incorrect.E: Apo B-48 mediates chylomicron secretion from intestinal epithelial cells into lymphatics.

educationalObjective: Apo A-I, present only on HDL, activates LCAT and is required for normal HDL maturation and plasma cholesterol esterification.
